correctness.rationale: For every k>=4 and q>=k, the exact grounded matrix has eigenvalues q (multiplicity alpha-1) and 2 (multiplicity beta-1) away from the class-constant 2x2 block, yielding J_h exactly, including both empty-class boundaries by direct evaluation. Direct subtraction proves J_1-J_2=(3-k)/(q+k-1)<0 and J_0-J_1=P_k(q)/(2kq(q+k-1)). The cubic has P_k(2k)<0, P_k(3k)>0 and P_k strictly convex on q>=k, so its sign changes exactly once. Taylor expansion at (1+sqrt(2))k-3/2 establishes O(1/k) asymptotics. Exact rational grounded inversions in verify.py independently agree on 258 class representatives and all 1474 small labeled sets. Computations do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: For a natural two-hub common-neighbor network, exactly classifies every globally optimal leader set for every integer k>=4 and q>=k, with a sharp q-dependent support transition and precise asymptotic q/k ratio 1+sqrt(2). The result reveals a counterintuitive structural fact: no optimal k>=4 set ever grounds both highest-degree hubs, while a concrete K_(2,8) two-to-four-leader upgrade replaces both optimal hubs with only peripheral leaders. These are design insights and a natural complete infinite-family classification beyond a numerical or arbitrary finite calculation. The calculation is not claimed to extend to arbitrary networks.
